forms[0].when: Add -는 to any verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. → Add -는 to the verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. (For ㄹ-stems, see below.)
watchOut 2번째 항목 (예쁘는 가방): Adjectives never take -는. They take -(으)ㄴ. → Adjectives (except words ending in 있다/없다) do not take -는. They take -(으)ㄴ.
forms[3].when (형용사 + -(으)ㄴ): Use this for any adjective describing a noun. → Use this for adjectives describing a noun (except words ending in 있다/없다, which take -는).

fixes.before: The action is happening now or happens regularly. Add -는 to any verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는.
fixes.after: The action is happening now or happens regularly. Add -는 to the verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. (For ㄹ-stems, see below.)

fixes.before: Use this for any adjective describing a noun. It shows the current state, so there is no separate present form with -는. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -은 (작다 → 작은). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄴ (크다 → 큰).
fixes.after: Use this for adjectives describing a noun (except words ending in 있다/없다, which take -는). It shows the current state, so there is no separate present form with -는. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -은 (작다 → 작은). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄴ (크다 → 큰).

fixes.before: Words ending in 있다 or 없다 (맛있다, 재미없다, 있다, 없다) always take -는, even when they work like adjectives in English.
fixes.after: Words ending in 있다 or 없다 (맛있다, 재미없다, 있다, 없다) take -는, not -(으)ㄴ, to describe a present state, even when they work like adjectives in English.

fixes.before: Korean puts describing words before the noun. Which ending you use depends on two things: whether the word is a verb or an adjective, and the time of the action. Verbs take -는 (now), -(으)ㄴ (past), or -(으)ㄹ (future or planned). Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ. Words ending in 있다/없다 always take -는. ㄹ-stems drop their ㄹ, and most ㅂ-adjectives change ㅂ to 우.
fixes.after: Korean puts describing words before the noun. Which ending you use depends on two things: whether the word is a verb or an adjective, and the time of the action. Verbs take -는 (now), -(으)ㄴ (past), or -(으)ㄹ (future or planned). Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ. Words ending in 있다/없다 take -는 (not -(으)ㄴ) to describe a present state. ㄹ-stems drop their ㄹ, and most ㅂ-adjectives change ㅂ to 우.

fixes.problem: 'Los verbos con raíz en ㄹ' limits the rule to verbs. The English 'ㄹ-stems' covers both verbs and adjectives (see 멀다 → 먼 in line 18).
fixes.fix: En coreano, las palabras que describen van antes del sustantivo. La terminación que se usa depende de dos cosas: si la palabra es un verbo o un adjetivo, y el momento de la acción. Los verbos llevan -는 (presente), -(으)ㄴ (pasado), o -(으)ㄹ (futuro o algo planeado). Los adjetivos llevan -(으)ㄴ. Las palabras que terminan en 있다/없다 llevan -는 (no -(으)ㄴ) para describir un estado presente. Las raíces en ㄹ pierden la ㄹ, y la mayoría de los adjetivos en ㅂ cambian la ㅂ por 우.

fixes.problem: The English "does / is doing" covers both regular actions and actions happening now, matching line 3. "正在做的" only covers happening now, so the regular (habitual) meaning is lost.
fixes.fix: 某人做的/正在做的(名词)

fixes.problem: The pattern gloss uses 했던 (-었던), a different grammar form, instead of the -(으)ㄴ past modifier this section teaches (하다 → 한). This misrepresents the pattern being taught.
The German is broken. „hängt von zwei Dingen ab: ob …, und um die Zeit der Handlung“ uses the wrong preposition in the second part: „abhängen“ needs „von“, not „um“.
fixes.fix: Im Koreanischen stehen beschreibende Wörter vor dem Nomen. Welche Endung man verwendet, hängt von zwei Dingen ab: davon, ob es sich um ein Verb oder ein Adjektiv handelt, und von der Zeit der Handlung. Verben nehmen -는 (Gegenwart), -(으)ㄴ (Vergangenheit) oder -(으)ㄹ (Zukunft oder Vorhaben). Adjektive nehmen -(으)ㄴ. Wörter, die auf 있다/없다 enden, nehmen -는 (nicht -(으)ㄴ), um einen gegenwärtigen Zustand zu beschreiben. Bei ㄹ-Stämmen fällt das ㄹ weg, und die meisten ㅂ-Adjektive ändern ㅂ zu 우.

fixes.problem: The words "in English" were dropped. The point is that these words look like adjectives from the English viewpoint. In Korean grammar they are not treated as adjectives here, so leaving this out changes the meaning.
fixes.fix: Wörter, die auf 있다 oder 없다 enden (맛있다, 재미없다, 있다, 없다), nehmen -는 statt -(으)ㄴ, um einen gegenwärtigen Zustand zu beschreiben, auch wenn sie im Englischen wie Adjektive funktionieren.

fixes.problem: "Demandez à votre professeur les mots difficiles" means asking the teacher for the difficult words, not asking about them, so the meaning has changed.
fixes.fix: Posez des questions à votre professeur sur les mots difficiles.
